direct_claims: This chart shows population by country for the year 2023.
It belongs to the domain of demography and global population statistics.
The chart indicates that data are available from 10,000 BCE to 2023, although the displayed view is specifically for 2023.
The source branding shows it was published by Our World in Data.
The subtitle states that the figures are based on data and estimates from different sources.
The chart groups countries by continent or region using the legend categories North America, South America, Africa, Europe, Asia, and Oceania.
The y-axis uses population units ranging from millions up to about 1.4 billion, indicating that the chart is intended to compare both very large and very small countries on the same scale.

The note says historical country data are shown based on today's geographical borders, which means long-run comparisons in the broader dataset are adjusted to modern boundaries rather than past political borders.

The chart includes both sovereign countries and at least some territories or small jurisdictions, as suggested by labels such as Macao, New Caledonia, United States Virgin Islands, Marshall Islands, and Vatican.

Several example labels visible along the x-axis include India, Spain, Madagascar, Chad, South Sudan, Switzerland, Finland, Uruguay, Equatorial Guinea, Macao, New Caledonia, United States Virgin Islands, Marshall Islands, and Vatican.
The data sources listed are HYDE (2023), Gapminder (2022), and UN WPP (2024).
